content.text:
Per the docs, don't insert 55k rows one-by-one or all-at-once via the client API — chunking helps somewhat but the real fix is a different path:

- **`apps/docs/content/guides/database/import-data.mdx`** (line 78): "When importing data via the Supabase API, it's advisable to refrain from bulk imports" — the JS client `.insert()` isn't meant for large batches.
- **`apps/docs/content/guides/database/tables.mdx`** ("Bulk data loading", line 354): "When inserting large data sets it's best to use Postgres's `COPY` command" — load a CSV directly via `psql`/`COPY`, e.g. `\COPY player_game_logs FROM './data.csv' WITH DELIMITER ',' CSV HEADER`.

So: if this is a one-off load, export to CSV and use `COPY`/`psql`. If it must go through the API, chunk into batches of ~500–1000 rows per `.insert()` call (not one row at a time — per-row round trips are what's causing your hour-long runtime) rather than one giant array.
